/Lotus/Language/1999/StoryCatchup1Body:
Amir! Thank u for helping me with this! Ur hacking skills are gonna help On-lyne so much! <3
U don't have to be a fan of their music to admit they deserve better, right? Poor guys :(
If we get a paper trail of the shady backroom deals between HitMaker and the Höllvanian government, we can give it to On-lyne. That way, they'll have everything they need to break their contract and get away from these users as soon as we get them home!
I hear their manager is old school. He's just now figuring out email cause he has to for business. Bet a tech wizard like u can hack his stuff no problem ;)
/Lotus/Language/1999/StoryCatchup2Body:
Good morning Director,

It is my pleasure to inform you that HitMaker Music accepts your offer. 

There’s a smokin’ young secretary faxing you our signed NDAs as I type this. Everyone here looks forward to hearing more about the Technocyte Coda project. As they say, nothing beats Höllvanian innovation!

This promises to be a fine partnership.

Keep up the good work,
Gregory V.
/Lotus/Language/1999/StoryCatchup3Body:
Good evening Director,

I’m happy to hear that the boys’ samples arrived safely. Hairbrushes from pop star dressing rooms leading to major technological advancement… It’s amazing, when you think about it! I hope you get what you want out of them. What was it again? DNA?

You’ve made incredible progress on the Technocyte Coda project in just a few short months. Nothing like loose regulations to encourage innovation, I suppose. Your broken eggs make the most delicious omelets. We love that about Höllvania!

Not sure how much sense I’ll be able to make of it, but please fax me the results.

Here’s to a bright future,
Gregory V.
/Lotus/Language/1999/StoryCatchup4Body:
Good afternoon Director,

Or is it morning in Höllvania? Time zones always mix me up.

Been thinking a lot lately about some words I saw in your Technocyte Coda debrief: predictable, standardized, and controlled. Music to my ears right now.

The only thing predictable about pop stars these days is their whining and complaining. Fame really goes to their perfectly coiffed heads.

How are things going with the Technocyte Codas? I can’t wait to meet these new and improved stars.

Hoping for good news,
Gregory V.
/Lotus/Language/1999/StoryCatchup5Body:
Good afternoon Director,

Given the boys' recent outbursts, I appreciate your concern that their presence won't soothe your citizens as intended.

I think it's an inspired idea to have the prototype Technocyte Codas replace the boys for spoken interviews. We'll use the scripts you provided, and I'll make sure no cameras are present. 

The boys will remain on standby for in-person appearances only. Here's hoping the Technocyte Codas will soon be able to replicate the boys' physical appearance too.

Apologies for the hassle,
Gregory V.

/Lotus/Language/1999Quest/QuestCompBadEn:
Drifter,

I can make no sense at all of these readings. Your site of temporal injection has somehow shifted. Your loop now encompasses the entire year of 1999.

Albrecht's interference is to blame, no doubt. What does he feel you need more time to achieve? He surely must have given guidance, however cryptic!

I can offer one service, at least. I discovered a clandestine blueprint among Albrecht's personal effects, for a Warframe so secret it was never named. It is yours.

Loid
/Lotus/Language/1999Quest/QuestCompGoodE:
Drifter,

Albrecht's gone. Rusalka too. I can't believe how close we came to oblivion. You showed us what we were missing. For that... thank you.

You still need to keep the loop going, though, don't you? Because it's not enough to put things right, is it. We need to keep them right.

Soldiers against the tide. Now and forever.

Arthur
/Lotus/Language/1999Quest/QuestCompleteD:
The triumph of the Indifference falls in snow and ash as the shattered corpses of The Hex lie in the midwinter cold.

Only the Drifter's spirit refuses to accept that the story is over. Somehow, the Hex are the key. But once the circle has been broken, what can heal it again?
/Lotus/Language/1999Quest/QuestDesc: The desperate hunt for Albrecht Entrati has led the Drifter to the city of Höllvania on December 31st, 1999. Despite the Scaldra lockdown in the face of the Techrot menace, the citizens do their best to celebrate. But this has all happened before... and ended in disaster.

Sol is high on this beautiful, bright summer day. The wind is the only sound that can be heard as it blows through the empty trees. No one gathers in the marketplace of the walled city of Cetorvaln, the great capitol of the Dominon of Höllvandeim.
((WHAT? CONFUSED?))
((JUST. WAIT.))
Children once laughed here, gathered around their parents, as they fondly shared the memories of past celebrations.
Lovers stole secret moments. Sellers hawked their wares. Memories were made. Not so long ago, Cedric Dawnsong stood atop the gallows and waited for his execution.
But now... no one is here.
The stage is empty.
Save for six figures. Standing before the empty gallows, its noose dangling in the air like an empty promise.
You are all awake. Whole. Healed. Back where you began. But not entirely, perhaps, yourself.
Cedric is the most changed. His armor, blackened. His sword, no longer a gleaming gold, but tarnished, rusted, cruel.
"You're late."

A figure is suddenly lounging atop the gallows as if he had been there the entire time. The figure in the black and purple cloak, with the blindfold. His leg is dangling off the gallows bar. Kicking it idly, he grins wide.
"Hey, kiddo."
"You're right about one part of that. This isn't a game. Games have variable outcomes." He flips a dagger in his hand, catching it by the handle.

"When you roll a die, you're meant to not know what you get." The grin on his face never waivers. "But what if you could always know the outcome? What if you could see it, as it was happening, before, during, and after?"

"Where was I? Ah. Cheating. I suppose it is, if *you* think we're playing a fair game. Since when have I told you we're playing fair?" He laughs. "Not once! Not once have I ever pretended the scales were even. I'm many things, kiddo. I'm not a liar."
"Where was I? Oh yes! A game. Since when have I told you we're playing a game?" He laughs. "Not once! I'm many things, kiddo. I'm not a liar."
"Ever wonder why I call you that, 'kiddo'? I do. I wonder all the time. I wonder about what I am. Why I am what I am. Why I was brought into this world."
He lays on his back atop the gallows and stretches out, utterly unconcerned by you and your weapons.
"But *why?* Why?!" He lays on his back atop the gallows and stretches out, utterly unconcerned by you and your weapons.

"I sat and I thought about this for the longest time. It's clear that your youth has nothing to do with lack of power." He snorts. "But then... I figured it out. You know what you never had in your youth?"
"Choice."
"Children don't get to choose. They don't get to decide when to wake up. What to wear. What to eat. What to think. What to believe."
"Oh, you might be given the illusion of choice..."
"Like this game."
"Like the life you lead."
"Like everything that has been put before you to get you here."
"But everything has been scripted. Written. Chosen for you. By those who believe they know better than you do, kiddo."
"Giving in to Entropy?" He tsks. "Too bad I'm not done with you. Or your friends."
"You can call me... Entropy." He thoughtfully regards one of his daggers. "I like it better than the other nicknames."
"Hardly! I'm simply making a point. Playing your role in the story is perfectly respectable."
"And in a way, you do. But have you ever thought about how they all lead to the same place regardless?"
"I'm no more in a wall than you are that stupid fish in a bowl." He huffs. "It's not my fault I have to tap to get your attention!"
"If you ever learned to zoom out far enough, and see it the way I do, it might truly depress you to see the reality of it all." He sighs.
Entropy shoots up from where he is sitting, still atop the gallows. "And it will go on for an eternity more! Endlessly looping, free of change, free of choice, free of anything that matters!"

Entropy shoots up from where he is sitting, still atop the gallows. "All I have left is the humor in it! The pointless humor of my eternally looping existence! You won't stop until you've taken all the rest away from me!"
"Why? Why! To protect the universe from me? From the thing you released into the world? At what cost, I ask?! How many more souls will you doom to this?!" He gestures at the world around him.
"To this... banality! To this... pointless game of dice whose outcomes will never change. Of conversations whose outcomes lead to the same ends."
"Lives, and loves, and deaths, with no meaning."
"All in the name of stopping...me."
His laugh that time is quiet. Almost broken-hearted. He shakes his head. "Am I really worth all that hatred..?"

"Honesty! Brutal honesty. How refreshing." He laughs. "Ah, to be your enemy is to be kinder than your friend, I think, if being your friend is to be condemned to a never-ceasing loop for all eternity."
"If being cared for by you means to be condemned to this... this, never-ceasing loop for all eternity?" He sneers. "Then I would like to never be considered a friend to you, Wanderer."
"So you would rather condemn all the things you claim you love and care about to... this, never-ceasing loop instead." He sneers. "Then I would like to never be considered a friend to you, Wanderer."

Wall wall wall lovely lovely wall

I was younger then, of course. Nothing cures you of the drive to 'do good in the world' than spending some time in it.
This is where it got me. Literally. I only came here to Höllvania in the first place because of the story.
Sorry. Sidetracked. Need to rant. Are you up for listening to me sound off about a pet hate of mine?
Ok. Don't say I didn't warn you. I have a theory I call the Hero Virus.

Oh, he was here first. But he made the mistake of telling me what was happening here, and I couldn't sit on it. So I place a call to my old friend Danny MacIlvoy and pay over the odds for a forged visa and passport. Because I need them in a hurry.

Not long after we all got the Entrati shots, I thought I had some kind of secondary bladder infection. Mate. I was up and down off that couch like a yo-yo. I even had Lettie hunting me down cranberry juice and mineral water.

I learned to build walls around my mind after that incident. Lettie sometimes finds meds that can shut the whole telepathic side of me down, just for a few hours. I have a stash of them, but I don’t take them unless I really, really need to sleep.

I just don’t let them know how much of their inner lives I hear, see and feel. I don’t go probing uninvited, whatever Lettie might think.

Arthur didn't want the boys to see him cry, and he didn't want to cry in front of my dad, so the only person left was me. His shitty big sister.

Everything I had ever been, every tender moment, every laugh, every morsel of Eleanor Nightingale blew away in that storm.
It felt my light fading, and I swear, a tiny tremor of satisfaction went through it. As if it was pleased to have crushed me. A flea under its fingernail.

When I was eighteen, a whole bunch of us had been out celebrating the end of the exams. We were all packed into this tiny car. Me lying across three people’s laps on the back seat.
Seb Cromley in the boot, whingeing. Christopher and Marco in the front. Every one of us was drunk off our arse on strawberry vodka and ratcatcher.
Marco ran a red light, a car coming the other way T-boned us, we rolled off the road and ended up in a ditch. I only know that because that’s what the policeman told me had happened.

They had to cut me out of the car. I wouldn’t stop screaming. It was the kind of hurt that leaves you with no crevice anywhere in yourself to crawl into to get away from it. You're being punished for existing.
I was helpless as a baby rabbit. Melted like a crayon. Gone. Just lay there and belted out scream after scream. I'd always thought of myself as a tough cookie before that.
Two days ago I was run over by a Scaldra APC.
That same old pain went flooding through me, but it wasn’t crippling anymore. It was like fuel, revving me up, making me angry.
I picked myself up, relocated my shoulder and tore that APC open with my bare hands.

Okay.
A. Child. Is. A Child.
Bear with me.

Stop me immediately if this isn't something you want to talk about.
The Zariman? What happened with your parents? This child has been through the same horrific ordeal you went through, right?
Hello, Drifter. I'm upset.
Two things.
I miss wine. I've not had real wine in so bloody long. All the wine in Höllvania got requisitioned by Scaldra command a few days into the outbreak.
Quincy and Arthur tried making prison hooch out of fruit ration sachets, but those of us who still had some dignity left said no. Rare moment of Lettie solidarity, that was.
The other thing, the much much bigger thing, is the future.

Away with you. Leave me to my fancy rocks.
I expect you have crystals I could only dream about.
Tell me, wise traveller, of the crystals of your time.
You say ‘you only find it in the Void' like people are popping in and out of the Void all the time. I thought it was this crazy-making dimension, not a seaside resort.
That's her name? I think I glimpsed her in your mind!
How beautiful and sad. What must it be like, to become a monument to your love?
The pretty geode lady. I suppose she and I are related now. There's a comforting thought.
I hope nobody chips little bits off them as a keepsake. That would definitely happen in my time.

Now that's familiar. There are these top-security bunkers under Ludston and Mancunia. The idea is, if there's ever a Radiation War, the fat cats and bigwigs get to hide down in their luxury bolthole and sip Mimosas while the rest of us get burned to a cinder up above.
Same old story, she said with a sigh.

It's funny. Everyone was so scared of a Radiation War when I was growing up. I remember the public service broadcasts that used to go out. Sombre advice about how to stockpile supplies, how to prepare a refuge room, and how you really have to bury any dead relatives even if you don't want to.
When I saw the reactor exploding in your mind, it took me right back to all those nightmares. I knew we had to stop it, whatever it took. I’d make the others believe you.

It’s not a Radiation War that’s waiting for this planet, though, is it? It’s the Techrot. One way or another, this loop’s going to work itself out and when it does, the rest of the world’s going to get infected.
I wanted to ask you something, but I’m not sure how you’ll take it, so if I’m out of order please say so.
What were your parents like?
I'm sorry. I stupidly assumed that because your memories of the Zariman were so vivid, you'd be able to recall your parents, too.
I forget how many lifetimes you've lived.
I'm glad. If you don't mind me saying so, it shows.
There's a warm flame of kindness in you, and I was wondering who had helped to kindle it.
I didn't think you'd had a soft upbringing. I suppose colonists need to be tough.
With those Orokin in charge, it's a wonder anyone turned out decent.
Oh dear. Well, for what it's worth, you made a bloody decent human being of yourself.
I only wish you could have had an easier time of it.
No, I'm sorry. I had no right to ask.
I was thinking about mine. I do it a lot, actually. I sit on my arse and wonder what Mum and Dad would think about how their kids ended up.
As people they were radically mismatched, which means they had the kind of relationship that burns hot and bright for the first few years and then collapses into a sucking black hole after that.

Incompatible, in a word. Dad wanted us to be independent, so he'd engineer situations where we had to be. Dropping us off in the woods with just a penknife, that sort of thing. Mum was always coming to the rescue. It was doomed.

Dad is ex-army. Jovial, little wrinkly eyes, speaks like a newsreader, so broken on the inside that if you picked him up and shook him he'd rattle like a bag of gravel. He's surprisingly easy to upset. I've tossed off comments that I thought were mild, then overheard him crying in the loo later on.
Arthur and I quickly learned to play them off against one another. You know how kids are.

Mum’s lot were richer, which meant she had a long leash. She didn’t go down the party path, wine and drugs and weeklong binges in Ludston flats. That was more Aunt Janice’s gig. Mum is more flowers, pottery hedgehogs, pot-pourri and everything being Nice.
Parents always overcompensate for whatever they feel their own parents did wrong, don't they?

Well, they're divorced now. They waited until we were out of our teens to do it, out of ‘consideration'. That was kind, don't you think? Forcing us to live in a bloody battleground of a house because Kids Need Stability or some such garbage.

Once in a while. We used to go back home for Solstice. Now that I do miss. Decorating the star-tree, crowning Sol, little kids going door to door dressed as Lua’s Three Aspects, roasting the bird… it’s sentimental, but I genuinely love it.

Mum and Dad always had a peace treaty for Solstice and they always respected it. On a good year they managed to keep from ripping into each other until after Third Day, even with the plum brandy flowing.
If you just felt a massive wave of homesickness wash over you, that was me. Sorry.
I try to keep the big emotions to myself but sometimes they just boil over like milk in a pot, and everyone cops it. Then it’s on to the old KIM for a round of apologies.
I was just wondering what they’d make of you. If we ever get out of this place, I’d like to rock up to Solstice dinner with my time-traveling friend.
I think you'd like it. You and Dad and Arthur could sit by the fire and trade war stories, and Mum could gently prod you about whether you were single.
HA! That just makes me want to do it more.
That's so sweet of you!
Oh Gods, let's do it. If we ever get the chance, we'll make it real.
Um.
I can just see Dad politely asking "so was it always death by impalement, or did they try to vary it up a bit?"
... I should let go of this dream before I try to make it happen. We are here, this is now, and there's still a war on.
Thank you.
This took a turn, she said, fanning herself.
I'm going to dream about this. Thank you.
Thank you for a beautiful dream.
I've got one more thing to get out of bed in the morning for, now.
Would you WANT to?
You are an absolutely exasperating person.
I’m trying to have a perfectly innocent conversation about parents, with no ulterior motive, and now you’ve gone and knocked me sideways.
Right.
Sorry.
Yes.
By all means.
I'm going to have to give this the serious consideration it deserves. FFS.
My mistake.

Yes. The one you said was going to be a waste of time, and that you were only playing out of pity for him, that's the one, isn't it?
He's a charming little imp. Why are you asking?
As much as the next person, I suppose. Why are you asking?
Which one of us is no longer "too cool" for the game, exactly? You or I?
Ah. I see. You are the chosen messenger, sent from the Thunderbolt King to enlist fair Eleanor. No doubt all sorts of roguery await me. Fol de rol and so forth.

We've all been there at one point in our lives... trying to wear a mask to impress someone and falling flat on our face because we can't see where we're going. And you and I had barely met when you asked. All right. You're forgiven.
I will do you a favour and NOT convey those words along to him. Word to the wise: treat him with more respect in the future in my presence.
Honestly, putting on a daft voice and play-acting for a few hours sounds ideal. Count me in.
Oh! I would like to be a wizard. Or perhaps a bard. Or perhaps both? Can you BE both?
Or I could be a swamp hag! So long as I get to wear a tight bodice, mind. Mother Mossytits will eat your bones, little manikin.

She’s Death. Also one of the Aspects of Lua, depending on which tradition you follow. She’s the one who comes and tucks you into bed once the knockabout day of Life is over, kisses you goodnight, and sings you to sleep.
Mate. Everything Entrati gave us, the power, the strength, the armour plated arses… I'd trade it all for one crumb of reassurance that death isn't the end.
... it was going to be.
Forget it. I'm sure you have more important things to do.

I’ve tried. I don’t feel good about admitting this, but sometimes when we’ve been out on patrol and there’s been fighting, I look into the minds of the dying and try to go through the process with them. If there’s any light at all at the end of the tunnel, I just want to see it.
I know. I KNOW.
I tell myself I was trying to help but the truth is I just wanted to see. You're right. It was ghoulish.
I did, once. What’s the harm, right? They’re dying anyway. It was this young Scaldra trooper. She was coming for me and I shot her in the chest.

I knelt down by her side as she gargled out her lifeblood and tried to tell her it was okay, the pain was coming to an end, soon she'd be with her family who had gone before, all the placid, pacifying stuff you think of when there's a deathbed service to be held.

She was terrified. What was left of her conscious self was scrabbling around like a rat in a water tank. When she felt me in her mind with her, she tried to cling on. She begged me to help. Underneath it all was this… I don’t even know what you’d call it…
Denial. She didn’t believe she could be dying. And why would she? She’d always been there before. How could death be taking her away now?

Every day of your life, you take YOURSELF for granted. You’re there when you wake up and you’re there when you sleep. You live out your entire life in a house made of You. You never once go outside, because you can’t.
Then one day, you hear the house being knocked down.
What would you have had me do? Call Lettie over? Heal the gaping chest wound? All because I saw what this one was going through, up close?
Yeah. I was scared shitless. As she felt herself slipping over the edge, I was sure I’d be dragged down with her. I could feel this undertow tugging at me.
With the Scaldra it's kill or be killed. They don't offer us the luxury of mercy.
I had to stay, though. I couldn’t abandon her to die alone.
Though I guess she did, in the end. I couldn’t take that last step with her.
I learned nothing.
No.

She did, though. She saw her mother’s face, the kids she went to school with, her cat, some cousin who drowned. But they weren’t presences, or spirits. Just memories, forced to the surface by a dying brain desperately hunting for something to cling to.

Then the house of her identity began to come apart around her. Right before she died, she opened her eyes wide. I think in that second, for the first time in her life, she truly understood what death actually is.
Look. Next time you feel the need to call me out on my bullshit, don't feel you have to sit through it first.
No. We think we know what it is, but all of our experiences are from the outside.
Nobody's forcing you to talk to me. Bye.

Her whole life she was like a woman living in a house with no lights, and all she had was a flashlight. She’d shine the light of her awareness on one spot or another. A memory, a task, an interaction.
She’d move from room to room, explore the cellars in her sleep, but always it would be a closed, finite process. Do you follow me?

Then when the house was demolished and her persona fell to pieces around her, suddenly the flashlight wasn’t shining on a wall or a book or a couch. It was shining up into the infinite sky. Her awareness blazed into the endless without the obstacle of herself standing in the way.
I've tried to tell myself that, many times.
I can't believe it was nothing more than the brain shutting down. It felt like the soul breaking free.

I know it doesn’t make any kind of sense. It feels so counterintuitive, the idea that we are a point of view first and a personality second. All I know is that’s how it felt to be with a human soul as it passed from life to death.
Look. Next time you feel the need to call me out on my bullshit, don't feel you have to sit through it first.
Nobody's forcing you to talk to me. Bye.
Comforted? I like the idea that something of us survives. I love thinking that death isn’t about being deleted from the universe, but having everything deleted that separates you from the universe.
I know.
Honestly, this is why I wanted to talk to you about void ghosts and Cephalons and all of that stuff from your time. I need to know if we ever get the chance to communicate with people we’ve lost.
Real communication, not some hologram crap. The kind that lets you know definitively what the person thought.
I see. Maybe there are some doors we can never open. Maybe that's for the best.
His name was Christopher. He was Arthur’s best friend.
We were engaged. I thought I was in love with him.
I’m sorry. I can’t do this. I’ll talk to you another time.
Right. I’m calm and as ready as I’ll ever be.
Can I talk to you about Christopher?
Arthur's best friend. We were engaged. I thought I was in love with him.
Thank you.
Because he’s someone I lost. Someone who was very dear to me.
Since you and I are a lot closer now (in so many delightful ways) you should really know what who you're getting involved with.
Please correct me if I’m wrong, but lately I’ve been feeling like you and I are more than just teammates.
I've seen inside your head, but you've not seen inside mine.
So, please brace yourself and bear with me.
You've made it pretty plain to me how you feel, which I appreciate.
We’re definitely friends. Maybe more than that. But we’re still pacing uncertainly around one another and waiting for the other one to make the first move.
I like you, very much. I trust you. You've had plenty of opportunities to treat me like a freak, like Lettie does, and you haven't done it. Don't think I haven't noticed.
I want to tell you about Christopher because I think you deserve to know.
There's a time to bail on a conversation with a friend. This was not it.
He was older than Arthur and me by a few years. I can't remember a time when he wasn't around. Our parents were friends, so he was always over.

He used to play at soldiers with Arthur in the scabby patches of woodland down behind the estate. Christopher was the commander, Arthur the loyal lieutenant. If they ever let me play, I had to be the nurse. Obviously.

I wish Dad had looked out at Arthur throwing himself on yet another pinecone grenade, dying valiantly to save his CO, and thought ‘hmmm, my boy's getting a bit too fond of this Army lark, maybe I should tell him getting shot up isn't as much fun as he thinks.'
Our paths crossing was a rare blessing in my life, yes.
In some respects, yes.
Probably not. He'd just have seen it as Dad testing him.
But I was trying to tell you about a bereavement here.
But allow me to wish it had not come at such a cost.
Especially when I haven't yet told you how deep the wounds go.
Not really the time to look for silver linings.

Anyway. Summer after summer rolled past. We grew to be adolescents. It was all very awkward and smelly and hormonal. There were parties and exams. Christopher went off to college. The dog died, we got a new one. Insert montage here.
Suddenly one day I walked into the kitchen, I saw this stunning young man in uniform in front of me, and I thought ‘phwoar' for the second time in my life.
'Pwhoar'?
It's a traditional Britannic expression of admiration. It should be delivered in a sort of low growl, puffing the cheeks out.

Mandy Jellicoe. My crush. She dropped out of school, dyed her hair, got piercings, hung around town in a leather jacket smoking cigarettes and glowering at anyone who came too close. I looked at her and I could feel my bones melt.
Anyway. NOT RELEVANT.
Yep. He was kind. Gorgeous. Strong. Easy to wind up, too, which was a big plus. Hell-bent on joining the army, though.

We didn’t see eye to eye on that. To him it was a calling. He’d be out there helping people who needed it, making a difference in the world. He’d bought into the whole manly hero line, just like Arthur.
Yes. I hate what it did to Christopher, what it's still doing to Arthur, what it does to so many like them.
I have nothing against morals. Gods know I even have a few myself. But the whole hero narrative is pernicious bullshit.
You can fight for a better world without buying into the hero bullshit!
The whole point of the Hero Virus is that it's a virus. IT DOES NOT CARE ABOUT THE HOST. It convinces you that dying in a cause would be fitting and noble, instead of being a tragic bloody waste.

‘Why do you want to go and kill people in the name of a Prince who couldn't give a shit about you?' I'd say to him. He'd be hurt, because it wasn't supposed to be about His Majesty's Service. For him it was about taking out warlords who hoarded food and forced their political prisoners to work in the Rubedo mines until they died of exhaustion.
I was confident I’d be able to talk Christopher out of his military service. If not talk, then snog him out of it.
... not really the time.
This isn't easy for me so please choose your moment a bit better
Yes, and?
I was trying to save his life. I was willing to fight as dirty as it took.
Do I need to spell it out?
I got caught up in the very web I was trying to spin.
Right. By then, of course, it was too late. I’d gone into this thinking I’d bewitch him, but the truth is, he bewitched me.
I’m sorry. I’m not going to be able to get through this without crying, so if I’m slow in responding, at least you’ll know why.
I told him I was pregnant. He offered to marry me. Stupid beautiful idiot.
No. But I thought I was. I didn’t try to trick him, if that’s what you were asking.
Arthur was skipping on fluffy clouds, he was so happy. The guy he saw as a brother was going to be his brother-in-law.

Then everything goes into fast-forward. Something about a pre-emptive strike. Borders and containment, risk of escalation, moral bloody mandate. Christopher’s deployed, Arthur’s already signing up, all the boys are off to the Crimson Watch and my mum’s still trying to arrange the wedding seating.
They killed him. The people we were supposedly there to help. They blew his vehicle apart with a bomb made from fertilizer and masonry nails.
I tell myself ‘at least it was quick'. ‘At least he didn't suffer.' But for all I know, he died screaming with nails in his eyes
Shit
Shitting shit
I feel like you haven't paid attention to a SINGLE THING I've been saying to you here
I'm not interested in 'at least...' He died in a STUPID way for a STUPID reason
I cried of course but all the time I was thinking ‘what did you expect, you STUPID girl, you KNEW what you were getting into, you KNEW this was going to happen'
Telling you about it like this, it just feels like corny folk song shit
My love he is gone off to war, sing fol de rol de dee, oh no he’s dead, I shall wander in the lonesome valleys and never wed another
And if you aren't listening to me when I talk about this, what else aren't you hearing? As charming as this has all been between us I... no. This was a mistake.
And if you aren't listening to me when I talk about this, what else aren't you hearing?
This whole bloody thing was a mistake. We're through.
Sorry. Get it together, Eleanor.
I think he’d have liked you.
Got to go tidy myself up. Talk again soon.
Sometimes I have to ask myself why you’re still here.
Oh Gods. Sorry. I didn't mean it like that. I'm just having trouble seeing MYSELF as the reason you'd tolerate all... this.
... are we talking about the same people here?
I mean… we know what we're doing now. We're containing the spread. You've done what you were sent to do. You don't HAVE to stay. And yet…
Oh, don't get cryptic. I'll feel compelled to worm the information out of you somehow.
... wait, did you just leave?
Well, now I’m wondering what I did to trick you. Or manipulate you. Maybe I put some kind of suggestion in your head.
And I thank the Gods for the day you joined us.

Well, now I’m wondering what I did to trick you. Or manipulate you. Maybe I put some kind of suggestion in your head. Or maybe there’s a secondary Techrot virus in your system that’s attracted to what’s in mine.
I'm glad you found what you were looking for. All rivers find their way to the sea, eventually.
Or maybe there’s a secondary Techrot virus in your system that’s attracted to what’s in mine.
Or maybe (deep breath) you actually like me the same way I like you. Could it really be that simple?
As families go, this one's a mess. But I wouldn't change it for the world.

I'll make a deal with you. Go and see Lettie, ask her to run you through a quick psych-eval, get to the bottom of whatever's REALLY going on here, and we'll just forget this conversation ever happened.
See? That was easy.
OF COURSE I FEEL THE SAME WAY
YOU ARE THE BEST THING THAT EVER BLOODY HAPPENED IN MY ABSURD LIFE
WHICH MEANS YOU’RE NOT GOING TO BE PART OF IT FOR LONG AND THE SOONER WE BOTH ADMIT THAT THE BETTER
BECAUSE THAT’S HOW IT WORKS
No. We’re not alone, are we? And we never have to be.
Right. I can see you've made your mind up.

I could come up with a dozen different reasons why we shouldn't be together, and you'd have an answer for every one of them. Oh, what if I infect you? You're immune. What if I try to eat you? You're functionally immortal. What if I see inside your head? I'm sure you'd just kick me out again.
You wonderful, impossible creature. You’ve only gone and won me over, you have.
Oh, one last thing. I don’t know if you’ve noticed, but I have this embarrassing personal problem. We do need to address it.
"I love to watch you sleeeep..."
That's more embarrassing for OTHER people.
Well I’m not talking about the size of my arse am I?
No. I'm referencing my tongue. The anaconda in the room.
Yes, the tongue. The anaconda in the room.
Tell me, honestly. How do you feel about it?
So... I'm not the first tentacle-tongued woman you've flirted with? Actually, don't answer that. I'm scared to learn the answer.
Right.
Oh! I see! You imagined you were doing me a favour!
Well. That’s that settled, then.
I appreciate your honesty.
I'm afraid the closest you will get to me now is if you set yourself on fire.
I'm scared. Excited. Nervous. Frankly, more than a little aroused. Might be getting ahead of myself there.
Shall we do this?
I wish you the best of luck finding a less 'gross' person to be intimate with.
In which event, I might bring myself to piss on you.
Of course. Let's do that, then.
Gods. I hadn’t even thought of that.
Right now I’m too happy to care, but I suppose we ought to tell them.
Hmm. I'm thinking seriously about pouncing you in Arthur's office and ‘accidentally' turning the tannoy on so that Lettie can hear every gasp.
Better not, though. Life’s traumatic enough as it is.
Hold that thought, lover. Let’s see where imagination takes us.
It's the loudspeaker thing. 'The Mall will be closing in five minutes, blah blah blah, shoplifting is punishable by summary execution.'
So help me, I do love how bewildered you are sometimes.
Dear? If you're there, I could use your ear.
If you’re there, I could use a friend.
I’m having the Arthur dreams again. The ones where he has to kill me.

I keep having this terrible dream about Arthur where he has to kill me. And as he shoves the blade between my ribs I'm screaming "Eleanor is RIGHT HERE, you stupid bastard!" but he can't hear me anymore.
That's just it, though. ‘You're not my sister anymore.' That's what he says in the dream. Then he stabs me through the chest with his toy sword.
We’re only little kids in the dream, if it wasn’t already messed up enough.
Not even to ‘put me out of my misery'? Not even if I was suffering?
Yeah. That's the worst part.
It's so vivid, so real. Like I'm remembering something that actually happened.
I can't. He's his father's son. He's all about doing the right thing, not the easy thing.
He's his father's son. He's all about doing the right thing, not the easy thing.
I'm sure. The future is quite inventive in its cruelty.
Everything.
But my concern here is with the past.
It's one of the many, many things we don't talk about.
I'm not.
I'm honestly trying my best to explain.
My father set the example for the way Arthur and I deal with issues between us. Or rather, the way we don't.
We don’t talk about what happened in Cavona, we don’t talk about Christopher and we NEVER talk about Granny Callie.
Maybe I shouldn't.
Maybe I should.
Maybe it’s time.
Do you want the whole story? Or shall I boil it down to essentials?
Granny Callie was desperately sick. Demented. Our father suffocated her to death with a pillow rather than let her go on suffering. I hope that's curt enough for you.
Granny Callie was our paternal grandmother. Callista Penrose Nightingale.

She had Pelham’s Syndrome. You’ve probably cured it by now (she said with an inward wrench). It chips away at a person’s mind. Instead of watching someone you love die all at once, they fade away slowly, by degrees, like an old photograph parching in the sunlight, or a video copied too many times over.

When she first came to live with us, Arthur and I were so excited. To us, she was the lovely old woman who smelled of violets and told stories where she did all the different voices. She gave us actual folding money on our birthdays. We thought it would be like a birthday all the time.

Then she started to go downhill. At first she was just forgetful. Then she started confusing us with other people. She called me Albertine and Arthur, Charlie. Demanded to know where Jimmy had run off to. We never found out whether Jimmy was a dog or a cat or a boyfriend.
Then she started talking to people who weren’t there. Then she started wandering the house after dark.

I remember going for a wee in the middle of the night and seeing her lurching towards me down the corridor in the dark, groaning, her face all twisted up and her hair like a mad clown wig. I couldn't stop screaming.

When it got really bad, she would lie in bed and shriek. We’d go out to school in the morning and when I turned down our lane, my heart would sink because I could hear her from ten houses away, still screaming, eight hours later.
Our dad used to talk about putting a pillow over her face. We thought he was joking, because of course he was, that's his mum.

One night she was screaming, and the screams just stopped. I got up and went to Arthur’s room. He was awake, of course. We sat together listening and listening, and then we heard the door to her room close.
Died in her sleep, Dad said the next day.
If he honestly thought it was for the best?
You have no way of knowing that. If Arthur honestly thought it was for the best?
I don’t know. Maybe. It seems a lot less likely now I’ve actually told someone.
You’re wonderful. Thank you for bearing with me. I needed to get that out.
Hello my darling.
Hello, mysterious and oddly compelling stranger from another time.
I haven't had the Arthur dream once since I told you about Granny Callie. I think you exorcized that demon.
But since we’ve been together, something else has been happening. It’s a bit awkward actually. I’ve been meaning to talk to you about it, but there hasn’t been a good time.
But that's not to say there haven't been OTHER dreams. Rather disturbing ones.
That wouldn't be awkward. This is.
Gods, I wish. Nothing so pleasant, I'm afraid.
Don't worry. It's not bad as such. I'm not frightened. It's just...
(Okay, Eleanor, deep breath, you can do this)
I think the Techrot’s jealous.
I don't, which is why this is so troubling.
No, not that one. Funny that everyone seems to have had it, though.
That's exactly what I'm afraid of.
(Okay, Eleanor, deep breath, you can do this)
I think the Techrot’s jealous.
Oh, how I wish I were.
Jealous of our friendship, yes.
Oh, how I wish I were.
Jealous of you for taking me away, yes.
On some profoundly messed up level, it thinks of me as its property. I was meant to be its breeding prospect. The Legacytes see me as a rival queen, you know.
On some profoundly messed up level, it thinks of me as its property. I was meant to be its breeding prospect. The Legacytes see me as a rival queen, you know.
Well, maybe if I were a full Warframe, the Techrot wouldn't see me this way. As it is, my cells are still fizzling, and it sees me as its own.
Well, maybe if I were a full Warframe, the Techrot wouldn't see me this way. As it is, my cells are still fizzling, and it sees me as its own.
Isn’t it bizarre? The jilted ex!
Yes. It wants me back in its gang.
Where I come from, you’d have to go and have a fight with it round the back of the local supermarket. I’m not sure how it works in your time.
This is your REAL family, it whispers. Become part of us again, severed sister. Be accepted.
Oh Gods, this is the awkward bit.
The dreams I mentioned before? I'm certain the Techrot's sending them.
Whatever that stuff has that passes for a mind, it's always been able to connect with mine. The thoughts it sends are always so crude and weak I can easily fend them off.
Most of the time it just feels like this frantic scratching at the back of my skull, like when you’re in the loo and there’s a cat trying to get the door open.
Right. My defenses are down, and it can reach me.
It’s been hitting me on the most primordial level, if you know what I mean. It wants me back. It promises it can make me feel ecstasy I’ve never known.
It will seed my flesh with the dripping cysts of new life. Because it thinks that’s what I want, you see.
Now that's the kind of talk that gets a Drifter absolutely covered with kisses.
I know. I think it knows, too, which is why it's so angry. It can't compete.
I'll sleep easier knowing you have my back.
It’s okay, my sweet. I’m not about to leave you for a suppurating mass of tubercular flesh with lumps of orphaned technology floating in it.
Just… if you see me looking especially dark-eyed and gaunt on any particular morning when we wake up together, please bring me a nice strong coffee and don’t press me for details?
Fancy giving the Techrot something to be REALLY jealous of?
We'll face it together, then. Side by side. Always.
We're family. Blood and found. Unbreakable.
You might notice the Mall feeling a little different this morning.

You are... seemingly the new expert in matters of this kind.

I have... faith... you will be successful.
Ah, yes. This is still on default settings. This is Loid. I should have... led with that, but matters here in the Sanctum Anatomica have been deeply chaotic of late.

You're asking, in a roundabout way, if all "things" from the Void are only here because we've willed them into existence.

I suppose? The parts of the Void that I have interacted with tends to already be imprinted upon. We have already given it some kind of shape or form. Or we have blurred the line too far between realities.
I believe that the challenges we face right now are dangerous. Extremely dangerous. And we should treat them as such.
Ghosts are real enough to cause us pain. But they can't be treated with a bullet. At least not one that I've found.

I... honestly don't know, Lyon. And I wish I did.

Apology accepted. This time. I deal with this kind of disrespect enough from everyone else around here. As fascinating as you are, I am not everyone's pincushion. I have better ways to spend my time.

A warning. I deal with this kind of disrespect enough from everyone else around here. As fascinating as you are, I am not everyone's pincushion. I have better ways to spend my time.

Removed. Detached. Uninterested. Unimpacted. Even when Gerivaine died and he was left to raise his little welp of a daughter on his own.

So you say. And yet I stand there like a fool, guarding them, listening to them talk on the subject of the reunion as though I remember it happening. Do you know how awkward that is?!
Do you know how awkward it is, having to stand there and pretend that I remember the reunion happening?! When I cannot for the life of me recall it?!

It is like standing at a gala when someone comes up to you and clearly knows who you are, yet you have no recollection of them in the slightest, but are forced to continue the conversation as if you do!
I was thinking once I was upstairs, I would start lopping off his family's limbs and start mailing them to him in jars, one at a time.
Do you have even the slightest recognition of the kind of hell you have placed me in?! Any at all?! It is misery standing up there like that, and it is all your fault!

While I am... slightly dubious of your reframing of your events as a tactical retreat, I admit I am... in favor of it, all the same, Drifter dear.
While I am slightly dubious of your reframing of the situation, I am... too tempted by this new future and what it might mean for me to resist it, Drifter dear.
Very well. I concede and accept your argument. Late as it may be, it has... been effective, all the same.
This "new lease" on my life. Very well. I concede and accept your argument. Late as it may be, it has... been effective, all the same.
I appreciate it. More than you might know.
Now, I believe we may move onto our next battle in the war, yes? The butler.
I, for one, cannot wait.
Expansion to new horizons was our only option now.
Transcript: It was Scarne, testy, cerebral and acerbic, who had first mooted the Plan back in the days before the War. "We must fly the nest, for the nest is on fire."
Through over-exploitation and reckless experiment, we had fouled the System beyond hope of regeneration.
The dread of a Sentient return was so strong in him that he could only imagine retreat to islands within the Void-sea.
VM: PUNISHMENT
How little credit we gave the Sentients for courage.
They willingly endured the Void's scalding fire purely for the chance to punish us.
He, too, inaugurated the cowardly Towers in the Void.
I found myself petitioned for opinions. As strategist, I was expected to comprehend the enemy.
VM: DIVISION
We had no word from our people stranded in Tau, and no way to know whether their signals were being jammed or they had been entirely obliterated.
The Sentients could have destroyed the Solar Rail Terminus above Tau at any time, yet the Rail was still active.
Transcript: After the first Sentient invasion of the System and the disastrous Orokin riposte, a curious silence reigned.
Why? What did they gain from leaving the gate open?
Were they united in their aggression, or did some yet hope for peaceful coexistence?
As one, the Seven bade me become a Devil with a trident of warheads, a sower with a satchel of rampant radiation.
How had we tamed the Infestation in our ancestors' time? Rip open the atom's heart like a rosebud, of course!
Transcript: Monstrosity and excess had served us admirably in the past. I was expected to apply them as war-tactics.
That was the day we learned the Sentients were not only capable of nullifying our technology, but also of commandeering it.

The flock of wicked little leveller-drones we sent out came winging merrily back to us still heavy with bombs, chortling in unknown syllables, detonating in the midst of the very motherships that dispatched them.
VM: FIRE
Many refused the data outright and deemed them errors, or lies, or Cephalon conspiracies.
Transcript: The losses were absurd.
VM: LOSS
Raised and glutted on Orokin subterfuge, it was easy for them to reject the truth now.
From that moment forth, they lived in a fantasy engineered for their comfort.
We were winning; the Sentients were in retreat; all who thought otherwise were traitors.
And how long before those worm-ships were themselves replaced by some new monstrosity?
It was insanity. How could I strategize around the behaviour of Sentient crab-ships, when no sooner had my tactics been perfected than the crab-ships were replaced by worm-ships?

Transcript: Many of the Sentients evolved between encounters, so we could never be sure that we would face the same foe twice. But others remained in consistent form, as if they had reached some plateau long ago.
VM: ADAPTATION
Perfected killers, they brought the same cold horror that a shark does.
All we could do was go backward. Progress had been fatal. Old traditions, time-hallowed paths of honor and discipline, were owed their due.
Alone, in private, I turned that weapon on myself. Oh, how I bled.
Transcript: I was effortlessly expert with many of our weapons, but I excelled in the use of one: the lie.
VM: LIES
I brandished it most often against my own troops. I whipped them to the bone with lies of duty and discipline.
I smothered them with the lie that the war could be won. I pierced them with the lie of my favour, my most esteemed regard for them.
Rostig. Something wrong in the cloning process, they said. What else could make a Grineer stay at his turret while burning alive? Even a rat understands self-preservation!
Transcript: Traivon. I watched you hurl your Railjack into Praghasa's maw. Distracted, feeding greedily on you and your men, she never noticed my own ship speeding away.
No. Your "defect" placed you above them.
VM: SACRIFICE
I remember your last salute. The fading. Then I blinked open the eyes that had been yours, and saw my gutted corpse dead in the mud.
You laid down your life for your superior officer. I felt your selflessness like a slap in the face.
Maryna. You gave me your body. Together, in that trench, we drank Kuva. My hands shook and my gashed throat leaked, but I kept enough drops down for it to take.
At least our defeat shall be beautiful. Memorable.
But against all expectations, they prevailed. Soon stories of outrageously improbable heroism filtered back from the Front.
The war was all but lost; the Sentients were unvanquishable; let us, then, create these strange and surreal warriors and arm them with weapons of ancient pedigree.
Transcript: At first, the Warframes seemed more of an artistic statement than a legitimate weapon.
VM: WARFRAMES
Warframes had appeared from the sky, angel-like, liberating captives and devastating Sentient strongholds. Even alone they were miracles; in groups, they were gods.
Little wonder, then, that they were seen as mere propaganda.
Or perhaps she thought they would abandon the scorched, polluted remains of the Origin System and leave her to raise a new kingdom of her own.
Transcript: "Peace?"
Regardless, peace would not be tolerated. So we set to work to undermine it.
VM: TREASON
Her voice was broken glass grinding in my ears.
Executor Nitokh was displeased. She had expected a glorious escalation, battle after battle, ending in the climactic ecstasy of the Orokin's demise.
After which she would emerge from hiding and… well, there I am left to speculate. Perhaps she expected to be invited into the Sentients' confidence.
Ballas was obliged to decide, and earn the scathing enmity of whichever cadre he did not side with.
I found, to my utter glee, that he was now the rose caught between two thickets of thorns.
For reasons I cannot guess, he chose peace; it was four to three, and so the ravening Sentients were suddenly allies and friends.
"One way or another, he shall come around," Nitokh promised, even as I was dispatched to seek out malcontents among the garrisoned Dax.
VM: DIPLOMACY
Transcript: Among the Seven Executors, Ballas had styled himself first among equals.
Ever the diplomat, ever the honey-voiced persuader, he resolved the grudges and disputes of the others.
The warmonger faction, headed by Nitokh, pulled one way. The pacifists, under Scarne, pulled another.
Transcript: Her madness was seductive because it was obvious.
All our senses had been glutted to numbness centuries ago. Yet she was still, in her way, fresh.
Out Tormis went and back Tormis came, carrying wondrous bejewelled memories of a new System and new worlds to settle.
Leap in, her eyes said to me, gleaming with the joy of some colossal cosmic joke.
One always knew where one stood with her - right on the precipice of the great abyss.
Through her demented visions I could escape the long, bleak stagnation of Orokin existence.
Eternal. Limitless in her hunger. She summoned me to her bath one evening. I strode across the mingling puddles of perfumed water and blood and stood dutifully to attention.
"I'm bored, Roathe. Let's kill all the other Orokin and take over."
VM: NITOKH
Roathe the bloody-handed. Roathe the ogre fattened on the bodies of his men. Spendthrift of lives.
Transcript: I understood from the start - both on the battlefield and in the bedchamber - the path to victory through seeming submission.
As if I battled only for the battle’s sake! No. The Orokin Empire must end.
Not even Nitokh knew my true heart. She thought I aspired to rule alongside her.
VM: SUBMISSION
Where the enemy finds you yielding, there you can be sure he will push; and so you may easily trip him.
"Lackey," they called me. "Lapdog." Nitokh thought herself in control. How subtly I guided her.
For that to happen, the war must continue. Only defeat, absolute and irrevocable, would topple those seven golden gargoyles.
In that pale, outstretched hand… a syringe. Glittering with freedom… with another chance… with another life.
Transcript: Coward.
I took it.
VM: OBLIVION

That is what they called me, isn't it? I've read the history books scattered about this dusty hall. A lie. They did not know the truth. That I was ripped away from my time before I could complete my work.
Coward.
I remember now. He approached me, in the Golden Halls. He wore a face I did not know. But that is not so very unusual for our kind. I knew his voice. I knew the way he moved.
Coward!
He asked me a single question. Did I truly believe that I could ever be forgiven for burning it all to ash?
COWARD!
COWARD!
Transcript: When the Sentients completed the Solar Rail to Tau, there was no grand ceremony. It simply began to work.
Ceremony was hastily created, of course, for no true Orokin can blow his nose without observing some pomp and circumstance.
A great fuss was made over the First Transport to make the Crossing.
It was Executor Tormis’s stately cruiser, and in the choice of Tormis as expeditionary could be read a collective rebuke to Executor Tuvul for the grotesque mishap of the Zariman Ten Zero.
The Sentient attack that followed rather spoiled the mood.
VM: CONNECTION
Within days a flotilla of colonist ships had departed, eager to set foot on the virgin shore.
VM: OROKIN
Transcript: For so long the Orokin Empire had no enemies. Its military existed merely to pursue petty grudges, house against house, Executor against Executor.
When the Sentients attacked, we knew a unity long denied to us. The Dax drew their swords against something other than an insolent peasant or a larcenous trader.
The Emperors, the deathless titular rulers of the Empire whose power was vested in the Executors, lurched awake on their dusty golden thrones.
War, magnificent war! At last, the Empire meant something. Defined by an extinction more imminent than the Sun’s eventual death, we drank deep of the nectar of life.
The Gilderglass Enchantress rose out of Ceres fog on lethal wings, a galleon laden heavy with drones and silver-armored myrmidons.
Circuitry fine as mist formed a delicate lace beneath their translucent plating.
Transcript: We did not expect to lose.
The Sentients made sure we saw the outcome. They sang, and our technology failed. Our warriors struggled and suffocated inside their shining suits.
VM: HUBRIS
The crew of the Gilderglass Enchantress roasted alive as she swan-dived engineless through the skies of Tau, a complex and costly firework.
So vast she was that she barely cleared the edges of the Solar Rail.
After the Sentients' first expeditionary strike, we had prepared a punitive counterblast.
We fancied we were coming up with new and titillating ways to dispatch a far inferior foe.
How we flattered ourselves. In truth we innovated desperately, knowing ourselves outmatched by our protean enemies.
Transcript: Now, I remember the developments of martial Archimedea were, at first, presented as entertainments.
VM: INVENTION
They tore through us like swarming children devouring their bloated mother.
Desiccated, crushed between the pages of time, we had simply been out-evolved.
Like debauched roués watching criminals put to death in an arena-circus.
They were cells in the body of a sprawling, malevolent mass.
The Sentients had been given a mandate to evolve, and their only model for the endpoint of such evolution was us.
Transcript: We did not think of the Sentients as a ‘them' so much as an ‘it'.
VM: SENTIENCE
They were returning to the Origin System not just to obliterate the Orokin, but to replace them and ultimately… perfect them.
We were, I think, too conditioned by our experiences with the Infestation - a hive-mind of quite a different order.
We faced legions hurled at us with no more regard for their individual lives than corpuscles have.
It was easily done. I was too glorious a figure to be suspected.
Transcript: Among the Seven I was - so I was told - considered Nitokh's plaything and concubine.
The blood of better men dappled me like medals. In secret I amassed weapons for Nitokh.
VM: COMMISSION
In the early days of the War they appointed me Vice Regent Grand Carnus at her goading, thinking it a jest.
How quickly their laughter turned to solemn applause as I brought home the news of one victory after another.
It was always the standard they still bore, glittering in its Orokin gold, and smeared in dappled crimson.
Transcript: Nothing quite speaks to the pomposity with which we creatures treat the carnage of war quite as succinctly as the bannermen.
Laughable though that is.
I always ensured it stood proud upon the field before I departed.
VM: STANDARD
Those who must be protected at all costs - and followed without question.
And who may be threatened, I might add, to follow orders that no sane soldier would ever complete, lest they somehow come to suffer some more terrible fate.
It was always their forms my eye was drawn to amongst the rest, though their mangled bodies were no different from any other.
Childhood friends now in charge of legions of Dax, of Grineer, null-matter cells, self-replicating carcinators, primitive biodrone blade-spiders, canisters of low-tech troops.
Transcript: I recall them now. Coteries of laughing Orokin youth.
Nobility clad in the as-yet-unspoiled raiments of command.
Golden boys and girls with ravening devils at their beck.
Their arrogance trickles like stinging sweat into my mind. They drank and sang, boasting of the times to come.
VM: COMMANDERS
They would make names for themselves. Raise their families high in honor.
So many of them fell. Not even their bodies were returned.
To prevent the enemy from gleaning our secrets, they were Kuva-jolted to liquefy upon death.
The hope of a generation turned to an oily puddle, sloshed through by Grineer boots.

Lettie and I are friendly now. I think.
She seems to be very curious about religion in the future. She seems really into protecting animals, which makes sense with her pet rats.
She's always working really long hours to help the civilians. I wonder if there's anything I could get her that'd make her day a little easier...
Lettie is starting to like me, and it's getting easier to talk to her.
She has a real vendetta against Entrati, and she hates being stuck here. I'm hoping I can help her come to terms with this in time.
She's always so tired. I wonder if a bit of caffeine might help her in the mornings.
I've earned Lettie's trust, but I think that's also an easy thing to lose.
Now that she trusts me, it's much easier to talk to her. I can banter with her more, and she and I are much more on the same page. She has a wicked sense of humor.
You can never have too much coffee, right? Or at least that's what I've been told...
Lettie and I are close.
She's tough as nails, but she's also lonely. I might identify with that. I might not.
I think getting her a better coffee setup in the morning might be appreciated. Maybe some bedding for her rats? And medkits are always in short supply...
We're best friends. I know that no matter where I am, where I go, or what I do... she's got my back.
Although we're best friends now, I don't think romance will ever be an option between us.
Lettie told me she loves me. And I love her in return. I know that no matter where I am, where I go, or what I do... not even the Indifference can touch that.
We're dating. But I think we're still in a situation where I could mess things up.
I seem to have really messed things up with her. I don't think romance is an option anymore, unfortunately.
I think she might go out with me now if I asked...
/Lotus/Language/1999Texting/Romance/Lyon: Lyon is finally talking to me. I hope I can prove to him that I was worth the risk.
He has been through so much...
It will continue to be hard to earn Lyon's trust, but I think I'm making progress.
He is easier to anger than Marie, however. I have to be a little more careful with him.
Lyon and I are close now.
Lyon and I are the best of friends. I am honored to be someone he trusts so closely.
Though we are boon companions, romance is closed off to me, I'm afraid.
Lyon has confessed his love for me, and I for him. I could not be happier!
I've done something to either upset Lyon, or I've run out of opportunities to move forward with him. Unfortunately, there's only one way forward for me now...
I think I upset Lyon by not being willing to hear him out. I don't think I can go any further in meaningful conversations with him...
Lyon and I are in a romance. But I must be careful not to make mistake.
I don't think Lyon will help me reunite Loid with the Entrati family. I wonder if Roathe can help me with this...
Lyon has agreed to help me reunite Loid with the Entrati family.
Unfortunately, I made a mistake. Romance is now out of the question with Lyon...
Lyon isn't talking to me yet. I think the way to earn his trust is through Marie.
I think he would consider a romance with me if I asked...
/Lotus/Language/1999Texting/Romance/Mari: Marie seems curious about who I am and the future she finds herself in. She also seems deeply devoted to Entrati, who she knows as "le Cardinal."
Marie and Roathe do not seem to get along. And it seems if I want to get Lyon to talk to me, Marie is the path to that.
Marie and I are growing more and more friendly. She is welcoming and accepting, and open to honest conversation.
She is still completely devoted to "le Cardinal."
I am getting the sense that Marie really likes talking to me. It's mutual.
She and I are discussing ways to reunite Loid with the Entrati family upstairs. But it will be complicated...
Marie has started to trust me, I think.
She is still adamantly devoted to "le Cardinal," Entrati.
Marie and I have finally grown close.
Marie and I are the best of friends. I couldn't be happier.
While we are forever companions, I think any hope of romance is out of the question.
Marie has told me she loves me! And I have told her the same. I could not be happier!
I've done something to either upset Marie, or I've run out of opportunities to move forward with her. Unfortunately, there's only one way forward for me now...
We're in a romance, but I must be cautious. I could still misstep and ruin things if I am not careful.
I convinced Marie that Entrati is a complicated man.
Marie and I will never see eye-to-eye about Entrati. I made her angry, and now she refuses to help me unite Loid and the Entrati Family.
Marie and I will never see eye-to-eye about Entrati, but at least we have agreed we can move forward anyway.
Marie refuses to help me unite Loid and the Entrati family. I wonder if Lyon or Roathe could help me solve this...
Marie has agreed to help me unite Loid and the Entrati family.
Unfortunately, I think I said something to upset her very badly. Any hope of romance is now out of the question, unless Roathe or Lyon could help me...
I think she might consider a romance with me if I asked her.
/Lotus/Language/1999Texting/Romance/MinV: These are the people who raised Rusalka?! Suddenly everything makes so much more sense...
I've heard about "bickering like an old married couple" but, yikes.
Velimir likes to joke around. Minerva very much does not. I wonder how they ever managed to coexist.
They're here looking for answers about what happened to Rusalka and why. I wish I had more to give.
There's so much history between these two.
Velimir is clearly not over Minerva. I wonder if Minerva is just better at hiding her feelings, or if she's really as hard as she seems?
Velimir's a natural storyteller. But I can see why never being serious could get on somebody's nerves after a while.
They took the protoframe injections willingly. I wonder how many more are out there...?
They had no idea Rusalka lost her arm. I wonder when and how that happened.
Velimir is definitely going to liven up the joint. For better or worse. I hope Arthur knows what he's getting himself into around the big guy.
Minerva is really starting to warm up. She's starting to trust me with more personal details, and sharing "confidential" things.
I can see how they were once in love... I wonder if, deep down, they still are.
They're settling in. Which is really good to see.
Velimir is definitely going to liven up the joint. For better or worse. I hope Arthur knows what he's getting himself into around the big guy.
Minerva is really starting to warm up. She's starting to trust me with more personal details, and sharing "confidential" things.
Unfortunately, sometimes some relationships are beyond saving, it seems...
Well. I did it. I got them back together again! Now if only I could get them to stop flirting so much in public...
I wasn't able to reconcile Minerva and Velimir's differences, unfortunately...
Against all odds, I managed to reconcile Minerva and Velimir's differences. Now, unfortunately, I have to put up with their flirting.
/Lotus/Language/1999Texting/Romance/Quin: Quincy and I don't know what to do with each other yet. We're very neutral. But he seems willing to talk.
It seems like he wants to see what he can get away with - testing boundaries? It's hard to say.
He loves to shoot holes in Entrati posters. Maybe he could use a few more.
Quincy and I are starting to be more friendly with each other.
He still seems to be trying to get things from me. I don't know why, yet. Favors? What for? He's a flirt with a great sense of humor, but he doesn't mind being shot down.
I think he's starting to genuinely like me, though I'm never quite sure with him. He's got more going on than meets the eye.
He's got a fiendish sense of humor, and loves to tease. Talking with him is a game of komi. He wants to play.
He knows how this city lives and breathes more than the other Hex. Gifts that helps him barter with the locals might go a long way.
I'm starting to trust Quincy.
I still feel like he's keeping me at arm's length, though I don't know why. He's still after all these favors from me. Why?
He knows how to smooth things out with the locals. Getting him expensive goods that the locals might want to trade for, could be useful.
I'm pretty sure he'd go out with me if I asked...
Quincy and I are close now. Things are real, between us, I think for the first time.
He has a big heart underneath all that armor - protoframe and otherwise. He wants to just know he's not going to get used and abandoned. Again.
The people in the city still want their expensive electronics, even though they know it's contraband. He knows how to trade for it. Getting him those goods might go a long way.
Things seem stalled between Quincy and I. I think we're at some kind of impasse.
We're best friends. I know that no matter where I am, where I go, or what I do... he's got my back.
Although we're best friends now, I don't think romance will ever be an option between us.
Quincy told me he loves me. And I love him in return. I know that no matter where I am, where I go, or what I do... not even the Indifference can touch that.
We're dating. But I think we're still in a situation where I could mess things up.
I seem to have really messed things up with him. I don't think romance is an option anymore, unfortunately.
/Lotus/Language/1999Texting/Romance/Rese: Techrot Overload; Would You Like to Forget?
/Lotus/Language/1999Texting/Romance/Roat: Descendia Voicemails Unlocked: |VAL|
An Orokin. Here?! Where do I even start...
He wants to make a deal to reunite Loid and the Entrati Family. I had to take it.
He wants to make a deal to reunite Loid and the Entrati Family. I couldn't take it. I hope that was the right call.
He knows. Of course, he knows.
While he seems friendly for now, I'm still a bit suspicious.
He keeps calling me "Usurper."
I can't tell if he really likes me, or if he's just playing a game. But I guess that's just how Orokin are.
I think he's starting to actually trust me. He's starting to tell me things that feel... real.
I think he would begin a romance with me if I asked him...
We've begun a romance. But I have to be careful, his moods are sudden.
Roathe and I are the best of friends. Who would have ever thought that could be possible?
Roathe helped me unite Loid and the Entrati family. More impossibilities.
While we are the best of friends, a romance is out of the question between us.
Roathe has told me he loved me, and I have told him the same in return. Who would have ever thought that could be possible?
I've done something to either upset Roathe, or I've run out of opportunities to move forward with him. Unfortunately, there's only one way forward for me now...
I failed in convincing Roathe to face his truth. Maybe Lyon or Marie can help me?
I think I am at an impasse with Roathe. I cannot go any farther unless I disobey his orders not to go farther into his memories in The Descendia...
I failed in convincing Roathe to face his truth. Maybe Lyon or Marie can help me?
I failed in convincing Roathe to face his truth. There is only one option left to me now...
I think I told Roathe something that may have convinced him that I was in our relationship only for physical gratification? That may be why we can't progress...
Roathe has agreed to help me unite Loid and the Entrati family, he just said it will take some time.
Roathe has refused to help me unite Loid and the Entrati family. I wonder if Lyon or Marie can help me with this?
I have told Roathe that I love him...
I've made him angry. I fear chance of a romance with him is out of the question, unless I can cut some kind of deal to get out of it.
We faced his truth together, and I've convinced him he can remake himself into a better version of himself. He is no longer beholden to his past.
I'm in trouble... I can't tell him he's the reason we're in this situation...
We faced his truth together, and I've convinced him he can live his life however he wishes, free of the morals and scrutiny of others. I am excited to see what he's capable of.
I promised Roathe I would clear his memories of the truth he discovered. The question only remains... will I?

/Lotus/Language/Alchemy/HelminthEvolvedA: (I can secrete Infusions that will make you stronger, more versatile… but to do this, you must feed me… will you feed me?)
(When we’re both ready, yes. Your Warframe, my sacred kin, can be absorbed… ^It will blossom within my body, granting me a trace of its power. A power I can pass on to others...)

/Lotus/Language/Alchemy/Helminth_Tip0: Your Helminth needs to be fed resources. It will transform these into secretions.
/Lotus/Language/Alchemy/Helminth_Tip1: Your Helminth prefers a varied diet. Check each resource to find out how appetizing the Helminth currently finds it.
/Lotus/Language/Alchemy/Helminth_Tip10: Exercise caution when replacing Warframe abilities by means of the Helminth. Some Warframes have abilities that if removed, will lead to a loss of overall efficiency.
/Lotus/Language/Alchemy/Helminth_Tip11: Some abilities work differently when infused. Be sure to read their descriptions.
/Lotus/Language/Alchemy/Helminth_Tip2:
- No arrow means it feels neutral toward the resource.
- An upwards arrow means it craves the resource and can generate up to double the secretions from it.
- A downwards arrow means it is tired of the resource and will produce very few secretions.
/Lotus/Language/Alchemy/Helminth_Tip3:
Be mindful of the order in which you feed resources to your Helminth.
Feeding the Helminth a resource it finds very appealing, denoted by the upwards arrow, will improve its appetite for less appealing resources in the same category.
/Lotus/Language/Alchemy/Helminth_Tip4: Infusing an ability into your Warframe will replace one of its original abilities. You can only replace one original ability in each configuration slot.
/Lotus/Language/Alchemy/Helminth_Tip5: Your Helminth can infuse a different ability on each of a Warframe’s configuration slots.
/Lotus/Language/Alchemy/Helminth_Tip6: The Helminth can subsume a Warframe. This empowers it to infuse one of that Warframe's abilities into other Warframes. Subsumed Warframes become part of the Helminth and can no longer be equipped.
/Lotus/Language/Alchemy/Helminth_Tip7: You can use Augments for abilities you infuse into your Warframes. However, caution is advised. Some Augments require interactions with other abilities or passives, and if these are not present their benefits will not apply.
/Lotus/Language/Alchemy/Helminth_Tip8: Helminth will undergo Metamorphosis as it sees use, unlocking new features and unique abilities to infuse onto Warframes. Accelerate this process by feeding Helminth resources, subsuming Warframes and infusing abilities.
/Lotus/Language/Alchemy/Helminth_Tip9: If you change your mind about an ability infusion, the Helminth can always remove it.

/Lotus/Language/Alerts/ALDarvoMobileDefe: After provoking the wrong people, the independent 'merchant' Darvo had to go into hiding. Now he needs your help so that he can get his business back on track.
/Lotus/Language/Alerts/ALDarvoRescueDesc:
Tenno,

It seems I am again in a bit of trouble. Wait, before you go jumping to conclusions, I swear, this time it is not my fault. I used to belong to this organization, the problem is this organization has refused to accept my resignation. I guess certain people cannot live without my skills. This is understandable as I am very good at what I do. I just prefer to work without a plasma turret pointed at my head. I am sure you understand.

Now, I know what you are thinking. The last time you helped me you got a little more than you bargained for. Things worked out in the end though, right? Help me again and I will make it worth your while. Trust me.

Darvo

/Lotus/Language/Archive/AridFearBody:
RE: Secret Grineer Colony.

How do we hide it? The Tenno, with their eyeless slag, will squeeze it from our Scouts! They already know our methods from their Capture missions. Data-viruses distributed among our flock will not hold them off. Hiding the Grineer base and collecting our fees requires escalation.

My plan is simple. Gather our Scouts and Navigators and launch them in to the Void. This has two benefits: the Betrayers will be hard-pressed to assemble the coordinate data and if they do, they will place themselves at great risk aboard a conventional craft within the Void's storm.

If the board approves I will divide our flock into three groups and begin. It pains me to help the Dogs in this way, but as always, profit numbs the feeling.

Alad V
/Lotus/Language/Archive/AridFearComplete:
MY QUEENS -

They found us. Why did the Corpus think they could hide in the Void? Despite their heritage they seem blind to the Tenno's connection to that place. I know you are sour on mysticism but I'm beginning to turn my view on it.

Every time we tear a Tenno corpse from its metal womb we find nothing to explain their power. Our Warframe engineers gesture wildly about nanotechnology, how reactive dissolution hides the answers. What if a Warframe is merely a lightning rod? A conduit for these demons of the Void? Consider how it could change our plan.

For now I await the Tenno's invasion of our Settlements. I have brought with me some reinforcements and your messages of encouragement to rile up the troops.

VOR
/Lotus/Language/Archive/AridFearEscalati: We've decoded a segment - we are zeroing in on the Grineer Settlement. The Corpus are anxious to preserve their contract with the Grineer - they have dispatched new tools to the next segment of Capture targets...
